project.name: Trébol Shared Contracts
project.description:
Contracts published across service boundaries, consumed by the monolith and by every extracted service. Deliberately dependency-free: no Spring starters, no persistence, no web layer, and no Spring Boot repackaging - it is a plain library jar so that adding it to a module cannot change that module's runtime behaviour.
It currently holds the generated authority catalogue (org.trebol.security.authorities.AuthorityCodes), whose 54 codes are a client-observable contract embedded in every issued token. The catalogue is generated from business-rules-extraction/database-documentation/00-seed-data.json and verified against it on every build by AuthorityCatalogueIntegrityTest, which fails the build on any drift or unknown code.
Phase 4: the generator and that integrity test MOVED HERE from the monolith's test tree when the monolith was decommissioned. They have to live in the module that owns the generated artefact, because exit criterion X6 requires the catalogue to be a generated, versioned artefact - not merely free of literals. Had they been deleted with the monolith, AuthorityCodes would have silently become hand-maintained while still appearing to satisfy X6.
The test-scope dependencies below are the only ones in this module. They do not reach the produced jar, and spring-boot-starter-test is deliberately NOT used: pulling Spring in, even for tests, would undercut the point of keeping this module dependency-free.
